errors.english: and not just for the benefit of wandering beings, you possess the nature of diligence for the sake of exhausting faults
errors.why: The Tibetan says he strives to exhaust what is harmful (non-benefit) to beings; the English turns this into 'not just for the benefit of beings' and invents 'faults'.

errors.english: for the sake of benefiting wandering beings who have eradicated the dimness of ignorance
errors.why: It is the awakened one who uproots the cataract of delusion to benefit beings, not beings who have already eradicated it.

errors.english: He also understood the reality of mindfulness and the Vedas
errors.why: Paired with the Vedas in a king's eulogy, དྲན་པ is smṛti (the law-books / tradition), not mindfulness.

errors.english: He was the lord of the deathless ones, the guru of the gods, and
errors.why: This is the guru of the gods of the lord of the immortals (Bṛhaspati, Indra's preceptor), the term of a simile completed by འདྲ་བ on the next side; the king is not made lord of the immortals.

fix.find: He was the lord of the deathless ones, the guru of the gods, and
fix.replace: [He was like] the guru of the gods of the lord of the immortals [i.e. Bṛhaspati], and

note: Prose frame is sound, but several verses are misconstrued and the king's eulogy mistakes smṛti and the Bṛhaspati simile.

errors.english: concealing a remainder [note: a violation of monastic rules not fully confessed]
errors.why: ལྷག་མ here is a saṅghāvaśeṣa offence; the note wrongly defines 'remainder' as an incompletely confessed violation.

errors.english: ensure that they are quickly separated and released from the community's disciplinary actions
errors.why: The disciple helps the teacher quickly obtain (mnod) the penance etc. from the Saṅgha and quickly be freed of it; the 'quickly receive' half is lost.

errors.english: Even the one in reliance should not merely ask, but should provide assistance
errors.why: གནས here is the teacher of reliance (niśraya), who simply does not need to ask permission but should help the disciple; the English makes it the disciple and 'not merely ask'.

fix.find: Even the one in reliance should not merely ask, but should provide assistance
fix.replace: The teacher of reliance, for his part, simply need not ask permission, but should provide assistance

note: The pentad and ten-year passages are well handled, but the turn from the disciple's duties to the niśraya-teacher's duties is confused.

errors.english: Moon must be separated from his captivating mind one line of text regarding the King's reaction
errors.why: The English ends with a stray placeholder ('one line of text regarding the King's reaction') that is not in the Tibetan.

fix.find: one line of text regarding the King's reaction

errors.english: they said:
errors.why: The speaker is Moon, to whom 'the youths' reply in the next sentence; 'they' blurs who speaks.

note: Narrative is followed reasonably, but a scratch note leaked into the text and some verses are loose.

errors.english: (sanghadisesa) communal-remainder offenses
errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, so the Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa is meant, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.

note: Faithful account of the five modes of recitation and the duties; only the Pali term form needs correcting.

errors.english: Reasons 2 lines
errors.why: The side ends on the first syllable of gtan tshigs; '2 lines' is a stray placeholder, not translation.

note: The compound-analysing commentary is followed closely; apart from a leaked placeholder at the end it is sound.

errors.english: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena
errors.why: Right view etc. is the antidote that abandons wrong views and other non-virtues; it does not counteract their abandonment.

fix.find: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena
fix.replace: as the antidote that abandons non-virtuous phenomena

errors.english: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
errors.why: 'Noble, supramundane' qualifies the right view itself; the list of views begins with self, so 'noble being' and 'worldly being' are wrongly added as objects of views.

fix.find: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
fix.replace: It is the noble, supramundane [view] that is not motivated by views of a self,

errors.english: that which is prophesied
errors.why: In the series virtue / non-virtue, this is the (in)determinate (vyākṛta / avyākṛta), not prophecy.

errors.english: the primordial wisdom of seeing liberation
errors.why: The fifth skandha is vimuktijñānadarśana, the knowledge and vision of liberation.

note: Readable, but the opening antidote clause is inverted and the Akṣayamati quotation is mis-segmented.

errors.english: to refute those who would harm the self [note: by asserting its existence]
errors.why: བདག here is 'us / our position': the passage refutes an objection against the author's selflessness thesis (the compassion objection that follows), not people who harm a self.

note: The three-times and plantain arguments are rendered faithfully; only the transition to the opponent's consequence is misread.

errors.english: what is called substance consists of two types of meaning: the external object and the consciousness.
errors.why: Substance is the conditioned entity able to accomplish, independently, the two kinds of purpose connected with object and cognition; it is not divided into 'object' and 'consciousness'.

fix.find: what is called substance consists of two types of meaning: the external object and the consciousness.
fix.replace: what is called substance is that which can accomplish, without depending on anything else, the two kinds of purpose connected with the object and with cognition.

note: The account of remoteness, observation and the substance/quality debate is accurate apart from the definition of substance.

errors.english: the seeds of the abodes of living beings
errors.why: The third object, sprouts that have come up, is dropped from the list of things not made allowable.

errors.english: even as little as a single blade of grass
errors.why: རྩ་རྒྱུད here is a root fibre or rootlet (the smallest part damaged), not a blade of grass.

note: Accurate taxonomy of seeds and of the pāyattika; minor slips in the definition of the actual offence.

errors.english: giving to the one who instructs
errors.why: In this robe-distribution context འདོམས་པ(་པོ) is the distributor or apportioner of the Saṅgha's robes, not an instructor; the error runs through the passage.

note: A hard, terse Vinaya commentary; the order of the passage is followed, but the robe-distribution passage is obscured by rendering the distributor as an 'instructor'.
